jobs.summary: The Executive Assistant will provide comprehensive administrative support to the Deputy Chairperson of the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE). Responsibilities include managing schedules, official communications, documentation, budget management, and travel arrangements.
jobs.description: Provide administrative support to the Deputy Chairperson, including managing schedules, appointments, and travel arrangements to ensure efficient time management. Handle official communications, correspondence, and record-keeping for the Deputy Chairperson’s Office, ensuring accuracy and confidentiality. Assist in preparing and organizing meetings, conferences, and official events. Serve as a liaison between the Chairperson and other NEBE’s departments, regional offices and external stakeholders. Assist in managing the budget and resources allocated to the Deputy Chairperson’s Office.
jobs.rawText:
ORGANIZATIONAL OVERVIEW 


The National Election Board of Ethiopia (NEBE), re-established by proclamation No. 1133/2011, is the constitutionally mandated body to conduct elections, organize referendum and regulate political parties in Ethiopia. NEBE is working to boost its’ institutional strength with a special focus on enhancement of human resource capacity. Accordingly, NEBE would like to invite applicants for Executive Assistant position who meet the following requirements.

Required number:         One


Reports to:                     Deputy Board Chairperson 

Duty station:                  NEBE Head Quarter, Addis Ababa

Duration:                        Permanent

Discover more
Geographic Reference
Government Job Openings
Ethiopian Salary Calculator
Salary:                             As per the organization salary scale (Competitive)

Job Summary

The Executive Assistant in the Deputy Chairperson’s Office is responsible for providing comprehensive administrative support to the Deputy Chairperson of the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE). The Executive Assistant also plays a role in documentation, budget management, travel arrangements, and supporting specific initiatives and projects led by the Deputy Chairperson.

Duties and responsibilities

Primary responsibilities of the Executive Assistant:

Provide administrative support to the Deputy Chairperson, including managing schedules, appointments, and travel arrangements to ensure efficient time management.
Handle official communications, correspondence, and record-keeping for the Deputy Chairperson’s Office, ensuring accuracy and confidentiality.
Assisting in preparing and organizing meetings, conferences, and official events.
Serving as a liaison between the Chairperson and other NEBE’s departments, regional offices and external stakeholders.
Coordination and Communication
Coordinate with other NEBE’s departments and relevant stakeholders to ensure effective communication and collaboration.
Confidentiality and Integrity
Exhibit confidentiality and uphold ethical principles in all interactions and activities of the Deputy Chairperson’s Office.
Documentation
Ensure timely and accurate documentation of activities within the Deputy Chairperson’s Office.
Budget and Resource Management
Assist in managing the budget and resources allocated to the Deputy Chairperson’s Office, ensuring optimal use and adherence to financial guidelines.
Support to Chairperson’s Initiatives
Support to initiatives and projects led by the Deputy Chairperson, ensuring their successful execution.
Provides effective administrative support, contributing to the Deputy Chairperson’s successful leadership and NEBE’s electoral objectives in Ethiopia.
Any other duties as assigned by your line manager.
About You
Specification:

Education and Work Experience:

BA or MA degree in Management, Secretarial and Office Management, Public Administration, Law, Political Science or related fields.
4 or 2-years relevant experience.
Knowledge and Skill:

Strong organizational and time-management skills.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Attention to detail and commitment to confidentiality.
Ability to manage schedules and appointments effectively.
Proficiency in documentation and record-keeping.
Budget management skills and resource allocation.
Collaboration and coordination abilities.
Familiarity with event organization and coordination is a plus.
Requirement Skill

jobs.rawText:
Procurement Officer
 

About the  Job
Objectives and general characteristics 

Discover more

AIDOS is seeking a proactive and skilled Procurement Officer to ensure the efficient, transparent, and compliant management of procurement and operational activities. The candidate will ensure full alignment with organizational policies, Ethiopian legislation, and donor requirements, while providing technical support and guidance on procurement compliance to AIDOS project partners.

 Areas of Responsibility 


Prepare, update, and monitor the Procurement Plan in close coordination with Project Managers and the administrative management.
Schedule the timelines for tenders and supplies to avoid delays in project activities.
Identify and apply the correct procurement procedure (direct award, negotiated procedure/quote comparison, open/restricted tender, etc.) based on the guidelines and  spending thresholds set by Donor, Ethiopian Law and Aidos guidelines.
Prepare tender documentation: Tender Dossier, Request for Quotation (RFQ), Call for Tenders, technical Terms of Reference (ToR), draft contracts and any other document necessary to ensure compliance with Donor, Ethiopian Law and Aidos guidelines.
Evaluate and assess vendor proposals, ensuring that selected suppliers meet the project’s needs and comply with all contractual and regulatory requirements, such as the tax and legal standing of local suppliers (TIN certificate, renewed Business License).
Coordinate and keep minutes for Evaluation Committee meetings, preparing the corresponding minutes and Evaluation Grids/Reports.
Verify that all procedures comply with the Ethiopian regulatory framework (customs procedures, applicable taxes such as VAT and Withholding Tax, commercial regulations for NGOs).
Manage the documentation and permits required for VAT/duty exemptions and handle customs clearance procedures for goods imported from outside Ethiopia (e.g., Authority for Civil Society Organizations – ACSO / Ministry of Finance).
Draft contracts with selected suppliers and consultants, ensuring the inclusion of mandatory clauses (ethics clauses, anti-money laundering, AICS/EU audit rights).
Build and regularly update a qualified and evaluated Supplier Database.
Oversee the end-to-end performance of contracts from award to completion, ensuring proper delivery, physical verification, receipt, installation, and post-delivery services, while managing vendor disputes, non-conformities, or supply chain delays.
Prepare, update, and supervise the inventory management of fixed assets, equipment, and office supplies, ensuring proper physical verification, tagging, and record-keeping.
Ensure the complete, orderly, and traceable archiving of all Procurement Files, in both hard copy and digital formats.
Ensure the preparation of procurement documentation in view of internal and external audits (AICS audits, project audits, local administrative verifications).
Train local project partners on internal procurement procedures and donor regulations (AICS/PRAG).
Supervise and monitor partners’ procurement activities, ensuring compliance, transparency, and correct documentation management.
Provide technical assistance and ongoing backstopping to partners during purchasing processes and audit preparation.
Support logistics arrangements for meetings, workshops, training, and field visits.
Manage general office operations (e.g. vehicles, maintenance, stationery, rent, and other supplies).
And any other tasks required by the supervisor
 The Procurement Officer is available to perform any additional duties required by the Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative in line with his/her profile.

Supervision

The procurement Officer reports to AIDOS Country Representative and Deputy Country Representative

Education:በሜካኒካል ኢንጂነሪንግ፣ በማኑፋክቸሪንግ፣ በኢንዱስትሪያል ኢንጂነሪንግ ወይም በተያያዥ ዘርፍ የመጀመሪያ ዲግሪ።
የሥራ ልምድ፦ በብረታ ብረት ማኑፋክቸሪንግ፣ በትሬለር/ታንከር ገጣጣሚነት ወይም በብረት አወቃቀሮች ላይ ቢያንስ ከ2 እስከ 5 ዓመት የሥራ ልምድ።
ተጨማሪ ስልጠና/ሰርተፊኬት (የሚመረጥ)፦ (ISO 9001) ስልጠና።
አስፈላጊ ክህሎቶች
የመለኪያ መሣሪያዎች አጠቃቀም፦ Vernier Caliper, Micrometer, Ultrasonic Thickness Gauge እና የብየዳ መለኪያዎችን የመጠቀም ችሎታ።
ዲዛይን የማንበብ ችሎታ፦ የሜካኒካል እና የስትራክቸራል ኢንጂነሪንግ ስዕሎችን (Engineering Drawings/CAD) በጥራት የመረዳት ብቃት።

jobs.title: Part-Time Veterinarian / Livestock Project Consultant
jobs.education: Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) or equivalent Veterinary Medicine degree
jobs.summary: A commercial goat breeding project is seeking a motivated Veterinarian to support the planning, establishment and development of a new goat breeding operation on a part-time basis with potential transition to full-time.
jobs.description: Support the establishment of the goat breeding project from the planning stage. Recommend suitable goat breeds and breeding-stock selection criteria. Develop and supervise breeding and reproductive-management programs. Assess and select healthy breeding does and bucks for procurement. Develop preventive health, vaccination, parasite-control and biosecurity programs. Advise on feeding, nutrition and body-condition management. Develop protocols for pregnancy, kidding, newborn care, weaning and replacement selection. Monitor growth, health, reproductive performance and mortality. Advise on goat housing, quarantine, sanitation and basic farm infrastructure. Establish proper animal identification and individual livestock records. Develop practical farm SOPs and health-management procedures. Conduct farm, breeder, livestock-market and supplier visits. Train and supervise farm personnel on proper animal-management practices. Prepare regular technical and performance reports for management. Support the project’s gradual development into an efficient and commercially sustainable breeding operation.
jobs.rawText:
WE ARE HIRING

PART-TIME VETERINARIAN / LIVESTOCK PROJECT CONSULTANT

Commercial Goat Breeding Project

A privately backed commercial goat breeding project is seeking a motivated Veterinarian to support the planning, establishment and development of a new goat breeding operation.

The project will focus on establishing a high-quality breeding herd, retaining selected female offspring for herd expansion and raising male offspring for commercial sale.

This is a part-time position with the possibility of transitioning to full-time employment as the project grows.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Support the establishment of the goat breeding project from the planning stage.
Recommend suitable goat breeds and breeding-stock selection criteria.
Develop and supervise breeding and reproductive-management programs.
Assess and select healthy breeding does and bucks for procurement.
Develop preventive health, vaccination, parasite-control and biosecurity programs.
Advise on feeding, nutrition and body-condition management.
Develop protocols for pregnancy, kidding, newborn care, weaning and replacement selection.
Monitor growth, health, reproductive performance and mortality.
Advise on goat housing, quarantine, sanitation and basic farm infrastructure.
Establish proper animal identification and individual livestock records.
Develop practical farm SOPs and health-management procedures.
Conduct farm, breeder, livestock-market and supplier visits.
Train and supervise farm personnel on proper animal-management practices.
Prepare regular technical and performance reports for management.
Support the project’s gradual development into an efficient and commercially sustainable breeding operation.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required:

Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) or equivalent Veterinary Medicine degree
Good knowledge of livestock health, reproduction, nutrition and disease prevention
Strong interest in goat breeding and commercial livestock production
Willingness to undertake regular hands-on field work

Fresh veterinary graduates with strong interest and practical ability are encouraged to apply.

SKILLS & COMPETENCIES

Good understanding of small-ruminant health and management
Knowledge of breeding and reproductive management
Ability to evaluate and select breeding animals
Understanding of vaccination, parasite control and farm biosecurity
Knowledge of kidding and newborn-kid management
Basic understanding of livestock nutrition and feeding
Good observation and problem-solving skills
Good record-keeping and reporting ability
Basic Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets skills
Ability to work independently and take initiative
Good communication and farm-worker training skills
Willingness to travel to farms, livestock markets, breeders and project sites

Previous experience with goats, sheep or commercial livestock production is an advantage.

EMPLOYMENT

Position: Part-Time Veterinarian / Livestock Project Consultant
Initial Engagement: Part-Time
Career Opportunity: Possibility of Full-Time Employment

The selected veterinarian will have the opportunity to participate in the project from its establishment stage and potentially grow into a full-time technical or management role as the operation expands.

APPLICATION

Interested applicants should submit:

Updated CV
Veterinary degree/educational background
Brief description of any livestock or field experience
Short statement explaining their interest in goat breeding and livestock production
Current availability

To ammarabdellah26@gmail.com

We are particularly interested in veterinarians who are practical, curious, willing to work in the field and interested in building a commercial livestock project from the ground up.

About the Job
Role Overview
We are looking for an experienced Project Supply Chain Manager to lead and coordinate end-to-end supply chain activities for projects. The role will work closely with customers, suppliers, logistics teams, commercial teams, and internal stakeholders to ensure efficient, compliant, and cost-effective project delivery.

Key Responsibilities
Supply Strategy & Customer Collaboration: Understand customer requirements, align supply strategies with business objectives, and coordinate production and sales activities to ensure customer satisfaction.
Contracts & Solutions: Support bidding and contract negotiations, develop supply terms and solutions, and ensure that project contracts are supplyable and successfully executed.
Planning & Execution: Integrate project master plans, manage supply and demand, and coordinate shipping, customs, and other supply-chain activities to ensure smooth end-to-end delivery.
Logistics & Trade Compliance: Ensure compliance with applicable trade, customs, and logistics requirements and manage potential supply-chain risks.
Business Continuity: Identify and manage supply continuity risks and develop appropriate mitigation plans to ensure resilient project operations.
Resource Coordination: Coordinate internal and external resources, including suppliers, logistics providers, and project teams, to achieve project supply objectives.
Cost & Inventory Management: Drive efficient inventory management, optimize supply costs, and ensure strong internal controls and operational compliance.
Performance Management: Monitor supply-chain performance and take corrective actions to achieve project targets and customer commitments.

About You
Candidate Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business, Engineering, or a related field.
5+ years of relevant experience in project supply chain, logistics, procurement, or a related area.
Experience in project-based supply chain management and end-to-end delivery.
Strong understanding of demand/supply planning, logistics, shipping, and customs processes.
Experience working with customers, suppliers, and cross-functional teams.
Knowledge of trade compliance and supply-chain risk management is an advantage.
Strong communication, coordination, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
Ability to work in a fast-paced, international project environment

Job Summary

We are looking for 10 energetic, outgoing, and motivated Female Field Sales Representatives to join our field-based Sales and Marketing team.

This role is ideal for individuals who enjoy meeting new people, communicating confidently, and working actively in the field. The successful candidates will visit restaurants and food-related businesses across assigned areas of Addis Ababa, introduce our services, register businesses, and maintain accurate records using a mobile application.

Key Responsibilities

Visit restaurants and food-related businesses within assigned areas of Addis Ababa.
Introduce and promote the company's services to restaurant owners, managers, and relevant decision-makers.
Clearly explain the benefits of the service and encourage businesses to register and join the platform.
Register businesses using a simple mobile application.
Take clear photos of menus and accurately record food items, prices, and other relevant business information.
Conduct follow-ups with registered businesses when necessary.
Track and record daily visits, registrations, and overall field activities.
Report challenges, customer feedback, observations, and field activity updates to the team.
Maintain accurate and timely records of all assigned activities.
Compensation and Benefits

Monthly Salary: ETB 8,000 fixed monthly salary.
Daily Allowance: ETB 150 per day for transportation and mobile data expenses.
Registration Incentive: ETB 25 for each restaurant successfully registered.
Weekly Team Bonus: The highest-performing team each week will receive an additional ETB 2,000 bonus.
Team-Based Work: The role is conducted in pairs, allowing employees to work alongside a colleague.
Ideal Candidate Profile
The ideal candidate should:
Be confident and comfortable approaching people they do not know.
Communicate naturally, professionally, and effectively.
Handle rejection positively without becoming discouraged.
Demonstrate strong attention to detail when collecting and recording information.
Be proactive and able to take initiative rather than waiting for instructions.
Be energetic, motivated, and target-oriented.
Be comfortable working in a fast-paced, field-based environment.

About You
Requirements and Qualifications

Female candidates residing in Addis Ababa.
Confident and comfortable approaching and engaging with new people.
Strong communication, interpersonal, and persuasion skills.
Energetic and willing to work outdoors and travel between different locations.
Comfortable using a smartphone and basic mobile applications.
Must have a smartphone with a good-quality camera.
Reliable, responsible, and able to work effectively as part of a team.
Previous experience in sales, marketing, customer service, or field-based work is an advantage but not mandatory

The British Government is an inclusive and diversity-friendly employer.  We value difference, promote equality and challenge discrimination, enhancing our organisational capability. We welcome and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds. We do not discriminate on the basis of disability, race, colour, ethnicity, gender identity, religion, sexual orientation, age, veteran status or other category protected by law. We promote family-friendly flexible working opportunities, where operational and security needs allow. The FCDO operates an agile workforce and to facilitate this, you may be required to undertake other duties from time to time, as we may reasonably require.
Job Category  
Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (Programme Roles)
Job Description (Roles and Responsibilities)  
Main purpose of job:

The British Embassy in Ethiopia is responsible for the UK government’s efforts to promote sustainable development and support climate resilience in Ethiopia and deepen bilateral ties between the UK and Ethiopia. The British Embassy is committed to promoting economic reform and growth, investing in human capital, improving resilience to humanitarian shocks and tackling global challenges such as climate change.

This is a really exciting time to join the British Embassy, 14 months out from COP32 in Ethiopia.  This role will be central to supporting the UK’s partnership with Ethiopia on COP32, building on our global leadership on climate finance and experience hosting COP26.  As Climate and Nature Programme and Policy Officer, you will play a central role in delivering the Embassy’s bilateral Climate and Nature Country Business Plan and supporting the UK’s objectives in the lead up to and delivery of COP32. 

The role sits within the Climate, Economic, Trade and Investment Team (CETI), which leads the Embassy’s efforts on macro-economic reform, investment and climate change, including COP32. You will be managed by the Head of Climate and Nature. This role will also be part of the Embassy’s COP32 Unit.

The role combines high-quality technical policy advice with programme leadership and management. The jobholder will support the design, delivery and oversight of a portfolio of climate and nature programmes with a budget of >£1million.  The jobholder will ensure they are evidence based, strategically coherent and deliver value for money in line with FCDO programme management frameworks, while also directly supporting COP32 priorities.

The role will provide technical advice on priority climate and nature issues, with a particular focus COP32 priorities, climate finance, carbon markets, forest policy and international climate negotiations. The jobholder will exercise sound judgement in commissioning and undertaking analysis, synthesising complex evidence and translating it into clear, policy relevant written and oral advice for Embassy leadership, the COP32 Unit, FCDO headquarters and external partners.

The jobholder will build deep relationships and convene stakeholders across government, development partners and the private sector in support of COP32. This includes running the secretariat for the Climate Finance Taskforce under the CRGE Forum, supporting climate diplomacy, and building capability and coherence across the Embassy on climate and nature issues in preparation for COP32.

Roles and responsibilities:

Lead and coordinate delivery of priorities under the Embassy’s Climate and Nature Country Business Plan objectives. In particular, this will include delivery of the FCDO’s Carbon Accelerator Fund (>£1m UK investment per annum). 
Act as a key technical point of contact for the COP32 Unit on climate and nature policy issues, providing timely, high quality advice to inform strategy, engagement and delivery.
Provide high quality, technical advice on climate and nature policy, with a strong understanding of the Ethiopian context and relevance to COP32, including: 
o    Climate finance, including multilateral instruments such as the Green Climate Fund (GCF), Adaptation Fund (AF) and Global Environment Facility (GEF);
o    Carbon markets, trends and developments.
o    Forest management and international forest policy
o    Climate diplomacy and international climate negotiations, including the COP process.
Manage programme suppliers and delivery partners, holding them to account for performance, compliance and delivery of results in line with FCDO frameworks.
Run the secretariat for the Climate Finance Taskforce under the CRGE Forum, including expanding and managing membership, coordinating meetings, shaping agendas and driving follow up actions, with a clear focus on advancing COP32 relevant outcomes.
Build, maintain and manage a strong network of strategic relationships and partnerships in support of COP32, including at ministerial level, with national institutions, think tanks, NGOs, multilateral organisations and other donor partners.
Support and advance UK climate diplomacy and policy engagement with the Government of Ethiopia and international partners, including preparation for, delivery of and follow up from COP32.
Build capability and a shared understanding across the Embassy on climate and nature issues, particularly in the context of COP32, including through internal briefings, guidance and knowledge sharing.
Contribute to programme monitoring, evaluation and learning, including tracking results and supporting reporting against UK International Climate Finance (ICF).
Provide timely, high quality input into COP32 related ministerial and senior official briefings, correspondence and visit programmes.
Work collaboratively across the Embassy, with a flexible and adaptive approach to support on urgent business of the day. For example, providing support for meetings and logistics.
Essential qualifications, skills and experience  
Experience of working on climate and nature policy issues, including climate finance.

Excellent analytical and data analysis skills, and good experience presenting information in clear information products using relevant IT packages.

A proven ability to communicate clearly and confidently, verbally and in writing.

Strong understanding of Ethiopian climate and nature policies and architecture.  

Excellent inter-personal and team working skills, with an ability to multi-task, work flexibly and adapt to emerging issues.

Strong experience in relationship-building, establishing robust networks and managing partners or stakeholders is desirable. 

Familiarity with programme delivery or project management is desirable. 

Required behaviours  
Communicating and Influencing, Delivering at Pace, Seeing the Big Picture

Other benefits and conditions of employment  
Learning and development opportunities (if any):

The British Embassy Ethiopia wants to support all staff in their professional development.  We would be happy to support successful applicants in their climate career development, including working towards acceditation as an FCDO climate advisor.
Additional information  
Please ensure that your application is authentically written based on your own experiences. If AI tools are used, their usage must only be limited to specific tasks such as ensuring formatting consistency and keyword relevance. The core content, personal narratives, and responses to behaviour and skill-based questions must genuinely reflect your professional journey, experiences, and achievements. We place great importance on originality and individual effort throughout the application process. Any form of plagiarism will result in immediate disqualification.

The British Embassy will never request any payment or fees to apply for a position
The base salary is subject to tax and other statutory deductions
Employees recruited locally by the British Embassy in Addis Ababa are subject to Terms and Conditions of Service according to local employment law in Ethiopia.
All candidates must be legally able to work and reside in the country of the vacancy with the correct visa/work permit status or demonstrate eligibility to obtain the relevant permit
The responsibility lies on the successful candidate to:
1.Obtain the relevant permit
2.Pay the fees for the permit
3.Make arrangements to relocate
4.Meet the costs to relocation
Employees who are not liable to pay local income tax on their Mission salary may have their salaries reduced by the equivalent local income tax amount.
Information about the Civil Service Success Profiles can be found on this link: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/success-profiles
Reference checking and security clearances will be conducted on successful candidates
Please log into your profile on the application system on a regular basis to review the status of your application
Appointable candidates who were unsuccessful may be placed on a ‘reserve list’. If during the reserve period of 6 months the same or a largely similar role becomes available, that role may be offered to the second or subsequent candidate

Habesha Steel Mills PLC is looking for a dynamic and results-driven employees to drive business growth for our Steel Rebar products.

Position 1: Junior Sales Officer
Education: Bachelor’s Degree or Diploma in Marketing, Sales, Business Administration, Management, Economics, or related fields.

Assist in identifying prospective clients, contractors, distributors, and hardware stores.
Respond to customer inquiries regarding product pricing, availability, and specifications.
Prepare draft proforma invoices, sales orders, and dispatch documents under supervision.
Collect market intelligence, competitor pricing, and construction project information.
Support payment follow-up and financial clearance activities.
Coordinate with warehouse, dispatch, and finance departments.
Implement Kaizen and 5S workplace standards.
Competencies:

Clear verbal and written communication skills.
Willingness to learn and adapt in a fast-paced environment.
Basic proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.
Fluency in English and Amharic.
Location: Addis Ababa, Dukem, Hawassa

Position 2: Sales Officer
Education: Bachelor’s Degree in Marketing, Sales, Business Administration, Management, Economics, or related fields.

Experience: 3–7 years of professional experience in active sales, field marketing, or commercial distribution, preferably in manufacturing, construction materials, or heavy industrial sectors.

Key Responsibilities:

Execute sales activities to achieve monthly and quarterly sales targets.
Build and maintain relationships with contractors, hardware stores, builders, and distributors.
Prepare sales orders, proforma invoices, and dispatch documents.
Identify new market segments, construction sites, and retail outlets.
Collect competitor pricing, market feedback, and construction trends.
Follow up on client payments and financial settlements.
Implement Kaizen and 5S workplace standards.
Competencies:

Strong negotiation, interpersonal, and customer-handling skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and basic sales tracking tools.
Excellent command of English and Amharic.
Location: Addis Ababa, Dukem, Hawassa

Experience: 7–10 years of progressive experience in strategic sales, brand management, key account management, or commercial operations, including at least 3 years in a senior supervisory role within manufacturing, steel, construction materials, or heavy industrial sectors.

Key Responsibilities:

Develop and execute sales strategies to achieve revenue and product tonnage targets.
Design and coordinate marketing campaigns and corporate branding activities.
Manage relationships with key corporate clients, real estate developers, and major distributors.
Conduct market research on steel industry trends, competitor pricing, and major projects.
Supervise, mentor, and guide sales officers and field marketing personnel.
Liaise with architects, structural engineers, and institutional buyers regarding product quality and technical standards.
Champion Kaizen and 5S principles across commercial operations.
Competencies:

Exceptional negotiation and commercial skills.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, and CRM platforms.
Excellent command of English and Amharic.
Knowledge of additional local languages is an advantage.
Location: Addis Ababa, Dukem, Hawassa

Deadline: October 22, 2026

jobs.rawText:
Working at Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
As an international cooperation enterprise for sustainable development with worldwide operations, the federally owned Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH supports the German Government in achieving its development-policy objectives. GIZ promotes complex reforms and change processes.
In Ethiopia, GIZ has been working for more than 40 years in bilateral cooperation on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and on commission of the Ethiopian government and international donors.

Finance Specialist
About the Job
Climate Change Cluster
Job Title -Finance Specialist
Contract End Date –12.31.2027

GIZ is undergoing a reorganization worldwide and in Ethiopia in preparation for the S4GIZ-System. Starting January 1, 2026, the administration of GIZ projects globally will be managed through dedicated Service Units in collaboration with the respective country offices. In Ethiopia, three Service Units have been established, one for each Cluster.

The Climate Change Cluster Service Unit (CCC-SU) is one of these three Service Units created under the new S4GIZ-System. The CCC-SU will efficiently support 15 projects within the Cluster. Additionally, the Cluster will be responsible for managing the Service Units in the Regional Offices located in Hawassa, Jigjiga, Bahir Dar, Arba Minch, Jinka, and Gambella.

The CCC-SU is currently seeking qualified candidates for the position of Finance Specialist, with the duty station in Jigjiga.

Core Tasks:

 

Manage all financial job orders and assignments within the area of responsibility and serve as the primary point of contact for advising managers, project teams and staff on financial matters related to EU co-financed activities.
Provide specialist technical support to colleagues and project staff on EU co-financing requirements, financial procedures, budget management, eligible expenditure and financial reporting.
Ensure that applicable EU contractual, financial and compliance requirements are clearly communicated and appropriately applied within the project.
Coordinate and monitor financial processes related to EU co-financed contracts, financing agreements, grants and local subsidy agreements, ensuring compliance with applicable GIZ, EU and contractual requirements.
Monitor the implementation and financial fulfilment of agreements and contracts, including commitments, payments, reporting obligations and closure requirements.
Contribute to the development and improvement of financial tools, templates, procedures and instruments for EU co-financed activities and ensure that changes to EU and corporate requirements are appropriately integrated.
Ensure that financial matters within the area of responsibility are addressed promptly and professionally. Resolve routine issues in accordance with applicable rules and escalate complex financial, contractual or compliance matters as appropriate.
Contribute actively to continuous improvement of financial processes, internal controls and risk management within EU co-financed activities.
Ensure proper financial documentation and knowledge management, including maintaining complete and auditable records of financial transactions, contracts, reports, approvals and supporting documentation.
Support project staff, partners and recipients in understanding and applying relevant financial procedures and EU co-financing requirements.
Perform additional tasks as assigned by the line manager. Areas of responsibility may be adjusted according to the operational requirements of the Country Office and EU co-financed projects.
Main Activities

Finance Responsibility

Support the financial setup, implementation and monitoring of EU co-financed projects, ensuring compliance with applicable EU contractual requirements, GIZ policies and approved budgets.
 Manage and monitor EU funds, co-financing resources, commitments, expenditures, cash flow, receivables, payables and remaining balances, including the preparation of financial forecasts and expenditure plans.
Conduct regular budget-versus-actual analysis, identify variances and financial risks, and provide timely advice to management on corrective measures.
Coordinate and review EU financial reports, invoices, claims and supporting documentation to ensure accuracy, completeness, eligibility and timely submission.
Manage the financial aspects of financing agreements, grants, local subsidy contracts and other EU-related agreements, including payments, advances, settlements and closure.
Provide financial guidance to project teams, partners and recipients on EU financial requirements, eligible expenditure, documentation and reporting obligations.
Ensure effective internal controls, proper financial documentation and compliance with applicable EU requirements, including fraud prevention, sanctions and other relevant compliance measures.
Support and coordinate audits, expenditure verifications and financial reviews, and ensure timely follow-up and resolution of audit and internal control findings.
Act as the main financial focal point for EU co-financed activities, coordinating with service unit, Administrative Unit, project teams, partners and relevant EU stakeholders.
 Monitor financial implementation at Jijiga egional offices, provide technical support to regional teams and ensure consistent application of EU and GIZ financial procedures
  Maintain accurate, complete and auditable financial records and ensure effective financial risk management throughout the project cycle.
 

About You
Competences:

B.A. Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration or a related field.
Minimum of 5 years work experience in a similar environment
High degree of initiative, efficiency, team-working, integrity and accountability
Attention to detail and accuracy
Ability to work under pressure and patience
Thorough knowledge of GIZ instruments and procedures
Confidential handling of data and information
Previous experience in GIZ finance unit /GIZ Software’s
Qualifications and Experience:
Significant professional experience in financial management of EU-funded/EU co-financed projects.
Strong knowledge of EU financial regulations, eligibility of expenditure, financial reporting and audit requirements.
Excellent analytical, coordination, communication and advisory skills.
Fluency in English; knowledge of relevant local languages would be an advantage.
Requirement Skill

jobs.rawText:
Working at Hope Walks Inc.
Hope Walks Inc. is a U.S. based international non-governmental organization dedicated to ensuring that every child born with clubfoot receives effective treatment and the opportunity to live a healthy, active life. The organization works to eliminate clubfoot as a cause of lifelong disability by supporting accessible and high-quality treatment services.

In Ethiopia, Hope Walks implements a comprehensive program that focuses on strengthening the healthcare system through capacity building for health workers, provision of clubfoot treatment supplies, continuous monitoring of treatment outcomes, and increased community awareness. The organization also promotes holistic care for children and their families. Hope Walks Ethiopia works closely with the Ministry of Health and government hospitals to expand and improve clubfoot treatment services across the country. The program operates through a national coordination office in Addis Ababa and supports more than 70 clubfoot clinics nationwide, helping thousands of children receive life-changing care.

Finance and Admin Officer (Maternity Cover)
About the Job
 Position Title: Finance and Admin Officer (Maternity Cover)
Reporting to: Finance and Admin Manager
Location: Ethiopia
Employment Type: Four(4) Months Fixed Term Contract for Maternity Cover

Position Overview:
The Finance and Administration Officer plays a key role in supporting the Finance and Admin Manager (FAM) to ensure the effective delivery of financial,  and administrative tasks within HWs-ET. Beyond handling day-to-day transactions, the officer provides strategic and operational support to the FAM by contributing to financial planning, administrative systems strengthening. This position serves as a critical support function for staff needs, ensuring that financial and administrative services are delivered efficiently and transparently. By maintaining strong internal systems, accurate reporting, and timely administrative support, the Finance and Admin Officer helps the FAM to focus on higher-level management and strategic decision-making.

Overall, the position is designed to be a reliable partner to the FAM, ensuring that Finance and Administration functions serve the strategic goals of HWs-ET.

Key Responsibilities:
Financial Support (70%)
Maintain accurate accounting records, including cashbooks, ledgers, and vouchers.
Process payments, staff reimbursements, and supplier invoices in compliance with HW policies.
Assist in budget preparation, budget tracking, and variance reporting.
Prepare monthly reconciliations (banks, advances, payables/receivables).
Support preparation of donor financial reports and internal management reports.
Ensure financial documents are properly filed, archived, and easily retrievable.
Support month-end financial closing activities, including preparation of schedules and supporting documentation. Provide financial insights and analysis to support the FAM in decision-making.
Monitor outstanding advances, payables, receivables, and other financial balances and follow up with relevant staff to ensure timely clearance and settlement.
Perform other finance-related duties assigned by the Finance and Administration Manager (FAM) in support of effective financial management and organizational operations.
Administration Support (30%)
Manage office supplies, utilities, and administrative documentation.
Ensure and monitor that the office is clean and tidy for the employees.
Ensure proper record-keeping for contracts, agreements, and other administrative files.
Support travel arrangements, workshops, and meetings by handling logistics (venues, bookings, documentation).
Provide general administrative support to program and management teams.
Identify areas to strengthen administrative systems and propose improvements to the FAM.
Other duties : 

Please note this position description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the staff member for this position. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

About You
Required Qualifications & Experience:

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or related field.
2-4 years of experience in finance and administration, preferably in NGOs, INGOs, or donor-funded projects.
Basic knowledge of HR management practices is an advantage.
Quickbooks application is  mandatory and accounting standards (IPSAS) is desirable
Proficiency in MS Office (Excel, Word).
Strong attention to detail and accuracy in financial transactions.
Good organizational and multitasking skills.
Good communication and interpersonal skills.
Ability to provide strategic support and contribute to system improvements.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive HR information with integrity.
Team player with a proactive and solution-oriented mindset.
Competencies:

Attention to Details – Able to be alert in a high-risk environment; follow detailed procedures and ensure accuracy in documentation and data; carefully monitor processes; concentrate on routine work details, and organize and maintain a system of records.
Communication Skills – Able to clearly present information through the spoken or written word; read and interpret complex information; listen well.
Relationship Management – Able to develop rapport with others and recognize their concerns and feelings: build and maintain long-term associations based on trust; help others.
Initiative, Flexibility, & Problem Solving – Voluntarily undertakes additional responsibilities, remains open-minded and changes opinions on the basis of new information; perform a wide variety of tasks and change focus quickly as needed; able to take action in solving problems while exhibiting judgment and a realistic understanding of issues; review facts and weigh options.

jobs.summary: The Ethiopian Public Health Institute (EPHI) is seeking 4 data collectors for a 45-day contract to conduct a midterm assessment of the Minimum Acceptable Diet (MAD) among children aged 6–23 months.
jobs.description: Each data collector will visit randomly selected households, obtain informed consent, interview target groups, record responses on tablets, review questionnaires for accuracy, measure length and weight of eligible children, and ensure high-standard data quality.
jobs.rawText:
About the Job
Employment type: Contract

Duration: 45 days (with possibility of extension)

Required number: 4

Gender: Female /Male 

Report to:  Nutrition, Environmental Health and Non-communicable Disease Research Directorate

Salary: 25,000

Job Description:

The Ethiopian Public Health Institute (EPHI) strives to address nutrition- and health-related challenges through population-based research and evidence generation to support the effective implementation of the Food and Nutrition Policy and Strategy. In this regard, the Nutrition, Environmental Health and Non-communicable Disease Research Directorate of EPHI, in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and the World Bank, is conducting a midterm assessment of the Minimum Acceptable Diet (MAD) among children aged 6–23 months in selected Specific Purpose Grant (SPG) pilot woredas of Ethiopia.

Minimum Acceptable Diet (MAD) is a key World Health Organization (WHO) indicator for assessing infant and young child feeding practices among children aged 6–23 months. Adequate dietary diversity and feeding frequency during this critical period are essential for optimal growth and development and for preventing malnutrition.

Baseline data were collected in the selected SPG pilot woredas prior to program implementation, and the program interventions are currently being implemented. The midterm assessment is being conducted to assess the current prevalence of MAD and changes from baseline.

The data collected through this assessment will provide evidence on program progress, identify gaps requiring further attention, and inform the strengthening of nutrition interventions to improve complementary feeding practices among children aged 6–23 months.

Responsibilities:

Each data collector will visit the randomly selected Households from the list of eligible households.
Identify and obtain informed consent from the selected target groups for a follow-up visit.
The data collector will interview all selected target groups in the household and accurately record their responses.
Review each questionnaire on the tablet prior to leaving the survey respondents house and make sure all questions are answered correctly.
Data collector should be willing to stay at the study site until the end of the study period
Each data collector is required to ensure the quality and integrity of the data collected are of high standard.
Measure length and weight of eligible children
Each data collector is required to maintain good team spirit with team members
Each data collector should be willing to take additional responsibilities

About You
Job Requirements

BSc in Human Nutrition, Food Science and Nutrition, Public Health, and Nursing and related fields with 0 years’ experience and a graduate of between 2014-2018 E.C.
Able to understand the tools developed for data collection
Good communication and teamwork experience.

Salary: 30,000

 

Job Description:

The Ethiopian Public Health Institute (EPHI) strives to address nutrition- and health-related challenges through population-based research and evidence generation to support the effective implementation of the Food and Nutrition Policy and Strategy. In this regard, the Nutrition, Environmental Health and Non-communicable Disease Research Directorate of EPHI, in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and the World Bank, is conducting a midterm assessment of the Minimum Acceptable Diet (MAD) among children aged 6–23 months in selected Specific Purpose Grant (SPG) pilot woredas of Ethiopia.

Minimum Acceptable Diet (MAD) is a key World Health Organization (WHO) indicator for assessing infant and young child feeding practices among children aged 6–23 months. Adequate dietary diversity and feeding frequency during this critical period are essential for optimal growth and development and for preventing malnutrition.

Baseline data were collected in the selected SPG pilot woredas prior to program implementation, and the program interventions are currently being implemented. The midterm assessment is being conducted to assess the current prevalence of MAD and changes from baseline.

The data collected through this assessment will provide evidence on program progress, identify gaps requiring further attention, and inform the strengthening of nutrition interventions to improve complementary feeding practices among children aged 6–23 months.

Responsibilities:

Identify selected kebeles, EAs, and households to be surveyed in the selected woredas.
Facilitate household listing in the enumeration areas.
Develop a plan for the household visits and interviews and coordinate field workers' schedules in the selected kebeles
Ensure field workers have all the necessary survey supplies and equipment.
Ensure all the necessary survey supplies and forms are collected before leaving for the field and each day before going out to the field for data collection
Supervise daily data collection of the field workers
Ensure field workers follow instructions 
Assist in anthropometry measurements.
Assist field workers in obtaining informed consent from the study participants
Track the number of interviews completed each day
Check and approve the data collected by the field workers
Ensure the field worker sends data daily 
Provide feedback to field workers and answer their questions
Help resolve any problems that field workers might have in finding the selected respondents, understanding the questionnaire, or dealing with difficult respondents.
Report progress and problems to the field coordinator, project manager, and local authorities
 Should be able to take on additional responsibilities assigned by the coordinator


About You

Master’s degree in Applied Human Nutrition, Public Health Nutrition, Food and Nutrition, Public Health, or other health-related disciplines from a recognized academic institution, along with at least two years of professional experience and previous survey supervisor

Speaking and reading skills in Amharic and English are a must, other local languages skill has advantage.

jobs.rawText:
About the Job
Job Advertisement: Market System Analyst - Oromia Region

Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

Program: USDA Food for Progress (FFPr) 2025 – Partnership for Productivity (P4P)

Organization: Global Communities

Who We Are

Global Communities champions innovative solutions to complex challenges at the intersection of humanitarian assistance, sustainable economic development, and financial inclusion. We ensure our approaches are as dynamic and diverse as the communities we serve. We bring together local and global insights to save lives, expand opportunities, and fuel brighter futures.

About the Program

The Global Communities Food for Progress (FFPr) 2025, Partnership for Productivity (P4P) Project in Ethiopia, is funded by the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA). This five-year initiative is focusing on enhancing and strengthening of the livestock market systems in Ethiopia. The project aims to make the livestock sectors more productive, resilient, and profitable, thereby driving economic growth in the country.

P4P utilizes five integrated interventions that will be implemented in collaboration with both

US and Ethiopian private sector stakeholders. The interventions include:

Increase Use of Improved Agricultural Techniques and Technologies: Promote the adoption of advanced techniques and technologies to enhance agriculture and livestock productivity.
Increase Availability of Quality Inputs: Ensure Ethiopian farmers have access to high-quality agricultural/livestock inputs.
Trade Capacity Development: Support efforts to improve trade opportunities within the livestock market systems and value chains.
Increase Access to Finance and Risk Management: Expand availability to financial and risk management services to livestock producers.
Policy and Advocacy: Support policy and institutional reforms to create and expand market access for quality livestock production inputs and technologies needed by Ethiopian farmers.
The Opportunity

Are you passionate about strengthening livestock market systems and promoting sustainable development outcomes in Ethiopia? We are seeking one Market System Analyst for the Oromia Region to lead the implementation of market linkage interventions across the poultry, beef, dairy, and sheep and goat value chains. Reporting to the Senior Market System Analyst, you will work closely with public and private sector stakeholders

to identify opportunities, address market constraints, and strengthen linkages between producers, buyers, and other market actors. Through fostering partnerships and supporting market-based solutions, you will contribute to improved market performance, private sector engagement, and sustainable impact at the regional level.

Key Responsibilities

The Regional Market System Analyst will oversee market linkage interventions within the respective region to foster strong relationships and trust among producers, traders, processors, and service providers. The specialist will facilitate communication, partnerships, and both horizontal and vertical integration among producer groups, traders, aggregators, processors, and service providers to improve the availability and utilization of agricultural inputs, technologies, and services across poultry, beef, dairy, and sheep and goat value chains.

Primary Responsibilities

Facilitate market linkages among producers and producer organizations (e.g., poultry farms, dairy farmers, feedlots, milk collection and marketing cooperatives, producer groups, and unions), buyers (traders, aggregators, exporters, processors, etc.), and service providers (private veterinary pharmacies, feed mills, artificial insemination companies, financial institutions, insurance providers, feed suppliers, etc.).
Provide regular technical support, monitoring, and follow-up to livestock and livestock product traders, aggregators, processors, and input suppliers (including veterinary, feed, and animal genetics service providers such as AI companies), ensuring timely and accurate data collection, updating, reporting, and documentation using project-developed tools.
Collaborate with partners such as AfriScout and Heifer International at the regional level to integrate livestock market systems with market information, digital solutions, and access-to-finance interventions.
Support market systems assessments and updates, evidence generation for policy and regulatory engagement, and indicator tracking and reporting in close collaboration with the MEL team.
Support the organization and implementation of regional-level training, field demonstrations, trade fairs, learning events, and stakeholder engagement platforms.
Contribute to quarterly and biannual project reporting, annual work planning processes, and project learning and reflection sessions.
Serve as one of the regional focal persons for communications, coordination, and partnerships, representing the P4P project in the respective region.
Perform other related duties as assigned.

About You
Qualifications

BSc degree with a minimum of 10 years of relevant practical experience, or MSc degree with at least 5 years of relevant experience in livestock production, agricultural economics, agribusiness, agricultural extension, or related fields.
Demonstrated technical expertise in Market Systems Development (MSD), private sector engagement, and cooperative development and management.
Proven experience in building strong relationships and trust among private sector actors, livestock producers, cooperatives, and public institutions.
Strong understanding of the challenges and opportunities within poultry, dairy, beef, and sheep and goat value chains in Ethiopia, particularly within the target regions.
Experience working with donor-funded livestock development and marketing projects, preferably in the target regions, with prior experience in USAID and /or USDA funded projects considered an advantage.
Core Competencies

Teamwork: Works cooperatively and effectively with others to achieve shared goals and objectives.
Communication: Demonstrates strong listening skills and communicates information, ideas, and feedback clearly and professionally.
Adaptability: Adjusts priorities and approaches by gathering relevant information and applying critical thinking to manage multiple demands in a dynamic environment.
Collaboration: Open to new ideas, proactive in building strategic partnerships, and responsive to partner requests while ensuring compliance with procedures and requirements.
Leadership: Demonstrates the ability to work independently with minimal supervision while maintaining high standards of professionalism and accountability.
Why Join Us?

Be part of a mission-driven team making a tangible difference in Ethiopia’s agricultural sector.
Collaborate with diverse stakeholders and contribute to innovative, evidence-based policy solutions.
Enjoy a dynamic and supportive work environment.

About the Job
LonAdd HR Consultancy Plc (www.lonadd.com) is a Recruitment & Outsourcing Company based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, with branch offices in Dukem, Hawassa and Bahir Dar. We are looking to recruit a qualified candidate on behalf of our client.

Location    Addis Ababa at AHRI

No. Required – 1 (One)

Contract duration:- 1 year with the possibility of extension based on satisfactory performance.

Start date – as soon as possible

Background

Background and Purpose of the Position

The Government of Ethiopia, with support from the World Bank, is implementing the Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience (HEPRR) Multiphase Programmatic Approach to strengthen health-system resilience, preparedness and response capacities, including strengthening local pharmaceutical manufacturing and related technical and regulatory capacities. Within this framework, the Armauer Hansen Research Institute (AHRI), a national biomedical research institution with extensive experience in biomedical research, clinical trials and bioequivalence studies, is strengthening its capacity to support local pharmaceutical manufacturing and research. Under Council of Ministers Regulation No. 531/2023, AHRI leads bioequivalence studies in Ethiopia and is working to establish a fully operational Bioequivalence Center with Contract Research Organization capabilities within its new research complex, including appropriately equipped bioanalytical and clinical laboratories.

The purpose of the Senior Bio-Analyst position is to provide expert technical leadership for the design, establishment and operation of a regulatory-compliant and internationally competent bioanalytical laboratory within AHRI’s Bioequivalence/Bioavailability Center. The position will lead bioanalytical method development and validation, management of bioanalytical studies, analysis of biological samples and interpretation of pharmacokinetic data, while ensuring implementation of applicable quality, regulatory and safety standards. The Senior Bio-Analyst will also support laboratory-systems development, regulatory readiness, capacity building and adoption of appropriate technologies to strengthen AHRI’s capacity to deliver high-quality BE/BA services and support Ethiopia’s local pharmaceutical-manufacturing agenda.

Justification

AHRI requires dedicated senior bioanalytical expertise to design and operationalize compliant laboratory facilities, establish validated analytical methods and documentation, manage studies, ensure regulatory and safety readiness, adopt appropriate instrumentation, and build sustainable local capacity for high-quality BE/BA services.

Objectives Purpose and Expected Results

The assignment will establish and operationalize an internationally competent, regulatory-compliant bioanalytical laboratory; develop and validate methods for target molecules; support high-quality BE/BA studies and pharmacokinetic analysis; implement quality, safety and regulatory systems; strengthen laboratory infrastructure and technology readiness; and develop sustainable technical capacity within AHRI.

DESCRIPTION of the ASSIGNMENT

The Senior Bio-Analyst will provide technical leadership for planning, establishing and operating a regulatory-compliant bioanalytical laboratory within AHRI’s BE/BA Center. The position will lead methods and studies, support laboratory infrastructure and technology readiness, ensure compliance with quality and regulatory standards, and strengthen the laboratory team’s technical capacity.

Specific Tasks

Conduct a rapid assessment of current opportunities and foreseeable challenges in bioanalytical laboratory operations within the BE/BA industry and beyond, benchmark international best practices, and define the appropriate scope of laboratory services for AHRI.
Lead the design and layout of the bioanalytical laboratory and associated services and oversee necessary structural renovations.
Follow up procurement and installation of bioanalytical laboratory equipment, supplies, reagents and required technologies.
Ensure laboratory facilities have the technologies and resources required for efficient operation.
Implement quality standards so the bioanalytical laboratory and other BE/BA facilities comply with applicable regulatory and safety standards.
Lead preparation of SOPs and other operational documents in accordance with applicable national and international regulatory requirements.
Lead bioanalytical-method development for target molecules and prepare and review study protocols, reports and relevant SOPs.
Lead and manage bioanalytical studies, ensuring appropriate planning, implementation and documentation.
Analyze biological samples using LC-MS/MS and other relevant technologies and interpret pharmacokinetic data from BE/BA studies.
Coordinate with clinical teams to align bioanalytical and clinical activities with agreed study protocols and timelines.
Prepare for and participate in regulatory audits and inspections related to the bioanalytical laboratory and BE/BA activities.
Foster a collaborative and educational laboratory environment that promotes teamwork, learning and technical development.
Identify and propose innovative approaches to improve laboratory processes and strengthen data quality.
Train and lead the laboratory team, developing sustainable local technical capacity in bioanalytical laboratory operations.
Prepare regular progress reports and recommend improvements to strengthen laboratory establishment, operation and performance.
Deliverables and Reporting

Major Task

Conduct a rapid assessment of current opportunities and foreseeable challenges in bioanalytical laboratory operations within the BE/BA industry and beyond, benchmark international best practices, and define the appropriate scope of laboratory services for AHRI.
Lead the design and layout of the bioanalytical laboratory and associated services and oversee necessary structural renovations.
Equipment procurement, installation and technology readiness

Lead bioanalytical-method development for target molecules and prepare and review study protocols, reports and relevant SOPs.
Bioanalytical-study execution, sample analysis and pharmacokinetic interpretation.

Identify and propose innovative approaches to improve laboratory processes and strengthen data quality.
Prepare regular progress reports and recommend improvements to strengthen laboratory establishment, operation and performance.
Deliverables

Bioanalytical Laboratory Assessment Report - Opportunities, challenges, international good practices and recommendations defining the scope of BE/BA laboratory services.
Bioanalytical Laboratory Design and Operationalization Plan - Design, layout, technical requirements, structural-renovation recommendations and associated services
Equipment and Technology Readiness Report - Procurement, installation and operational readiness of equipment, supplies, reagents and technologies.
Quality and Regulatory Compliance Framework - Quality, regulatory and safety requirements established and implemented.
Standard Operating Procedures and Operational Documents - Required documents developed in accordance with national and international regulatory requirements.
Bioanalytical Methods and Validation Documentation - Methods for target molecules developed and validated, with protocols, SOPs and technical reports.
Bioanalytical Study Reports - Completed studies, biological-sample analysis using LC-MS/MS or related technology, and pharmacokinetic-data interpretation.

Regular Progress Reports - Progress, achievements, challenges and recommendations for laboratory establishment and operation.
Project Management

The Senior Bio-Analyst will report to the Clinical Trial Directorate at AHRI and coordinate with clinical teams, laboratory personnel, procurement and infrastructure teams, regulators and the wider BE/BA Center. Client will provide contract oversight through the institutional third-party HR service arrangement.

About the Job
Job Summary

Position Title: Sustainability Engineer
Duty Station: Based in Dera and North Mecha woredas, with regular field travel to rural water supply schemes and coordination visits to Bahir Dar as required.
Reports to: Sustainability Team Leader, Bahir Dar
Working Relationships: Woreda Water Offices, Professional Service Provider groups, community water committees, local government structures, and project technical teams.

Role Purpose

The Sustainability Engineer will provide technical leadership and field-level coordination to ensure the reliable, safe, and sustainable operation of rural water supply systems in Dera and North Mecha woredas. The position will support woreda-level operation and maintenance systems, oversee Professional Service Provider groups, strengthen data-driven decision-making, and work closely with Woreda Water Offices to improve water service functionality, accountability, and long-term sustainability.

Key Responsibilities and Activities

Oversight and Technical Support to Professional Service Providers

Oversee Professional Service Provider groups responsible for operation, maintenance, minor repairs, and service support activities.
Monitor PSP performance against agreed service standards, work plans, contractual expectations, and operation and maintenance targets.
Review PSP maintenance records, activity plans, spare-part use, customer support records, and performance reports.
Conduct routine field supervision visits and provide practical technical guidance, coaching, and corrective actions.
Facilitate regular PSP performance review meetings with the Sustainability Team Leader, Woreda Water Offices, and other relevant stakeholders.
Identify PSP capacity gaps and recommend training, mentoring, or management support to improve service quality.
Operation and Maintenance Follow-up

Monitor the functionality, reliability, and maintenance status of rural water supply systems across the assigned woredas.
Follow up preventive and corrective maintenance activities to reduce downtime and improve service continuity.
Ensure timely response to system breakdowns, including coordination of spare parts, technicians, PSPs, and woreda-level support.
Identify recurring technical, management, financial, or operational problems and recommend practical solutions.
Promote asset management practices, including maintenance planning, spare-part tracking, and documentation of system histories.
Support improved cost recovery, tariff discussion, and community contribution mechanisms where relevant to long-term sustainability.
Technical Assessments, Quality Assurance, and Risk Management

Conduct periodic technical and operational assessments of water supply schemes, including infrastructure condition, service performance, safety, and management arrangements.
Assess operation and maintenance practices, water point functionality, service reliability, and sustainability risks.
Prioritize systems requiring urgent maintenance, rehabilitation, capacity support, or management attention.
Follow up implementation of assessment recommendations and document progress against agreed action plans.
Support quality assurance for repair, rehabilitation, and maintenance of works carried out by PSPs or other service actors.
Identify and escalate risks related to water safety, environmental protection, community conflict, service interruptions, and weak governance.
Water Safety Support to Professional Service Provider Groups

Coach PSPGs on basic water quality monitoring, safe chlorination practices, and immediate corrective actions when contamination risks are identified.
Follow up implementation of water safety improvement actions, including source protection, drainage, fencing, cleaning, and repair of damaged scheme components.
Coordinate with Woreda Water Offices, health extension workers, and community structures to document, report, and respond to water safety concerns.
Lead routine sanitary inspections, water quality monitoring, and follow-up actions with woreda water offices, health offices, service providers, and community structures.
 Data Management, mWater Review, and Evidence-Based Decision Making

Regularly review water point functionality, operation and maintenance, and service performance data in mWater or other approved monitoring systems.
Verify data quality, completeness, consistency, and timeliness, and follow up gaps with PSPs, woreda staff, or field teams.
Analyze trends in breakdowns, response time, functionality, spare-part needs, and sustainability risks to inform decisions.
Support timely updating of water point records, maintenance actions, assessment findings, and service provider performance information.
Prepare simple dashboards, summaries, or data extracts for review by the Sustainability Team Leader and government counterparts.
Coordination with Woreda Water Offices and Local Stakeholders

Maintain effective day-to-day working relationships with Dera and North Mecha Woreda Water Offices.
Participate in WASH coordination meetings, joint monitoring visits, planning sessions, and technical review discussions.
Share relevant operation and maintenance, functionality, water service, and PSP performance information with government counterparts.
Follow up agreed actions with woreda stakeholders and strengthen government ownership of rural water supply sustainability.
Support woreda-level planning, budgeting, and prioritization for maintenance, rehabilitation, and service improvement activities.
Promote collaboration among PSPs, community representatives, woreda officials, and the project team to solve field-level challenges.
Reporting, Documentation, and Learning

Prepare accurate monthly, quarterly, and annual operation and maintenance and sustainability reports for the Sustainability Team Leader.
Consolidate information from PSPs, mWater, field assessments, community structures, and Woreda Water Offices.
Document achievements, challenges, lessons learned, sustainability risks, and priority follow-up actions.
Provide timely technical updates and practical recommendations to management for decision-making.
Maintain organized records of field visits, action plans, PSP reviews, assessment findings, photos, and key correspondence.
Contribute to learning, adaptive management, and continuous improvement of the rural water service sustainability model.
LOCATION: Dera and North Mecha woredas, Amara region

SALARY: Negotiable

jobs.rawText:
About the Job
Job Advertisement: Livestock Productivity Specialist – Oromia Region 

Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia 

Program: USDA Food for Progress (FFPr) 2025- Partnership for Productivity (P4P) 

Organization: Global Communities  

Who We Are? 

Global Communities champions innovative solutions to complex challenges at the intersection of humanitarian assistance, sustainable economic development, and financial inclusion. We ensure our approaches are as dynamic and diverse as the communities we serve. We bring together local and global insights to save lives, expand opportunity, and fuel brighter futures. 

About the Program 

The Global Communities Food for Progress (FFPr) 2025, Partnership for Productivity (P4P) Project in Ethiopia, is funded by the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA). This five-year initiative is focusing on enhancing and strengthening of the livestock market systems in Ethiopia. The project aims to make the livestock sectors more productive, resilient, and profitable, thereby driving economic growth in the country. 

P4P utilizes five integrated interventions that will be implemented in collaboration with both  

US and Ethiopian private sector stakeholders. The interventions include: 

Increase Use of Improved Agricultural Techniques and Technologies: Promote the adoption of advanced techniques and technologies to enhance agriculture and livestock productivity. 
Increase Availability of Quality Inputs: Ensure Ethiopian farmers have access to high-quality agricultural/livestock inputs. 
Trade Capacity Development: Support efforts to improve trade opportunities within the livestock market systems and value chains. 
Increase Access to Finance and Risk Management: Expand availability to financial and risk management services to livestock producers. 
Policy and Advocacy: Support policy and institutional reforms to create and expand market access for quality livestock production inputs and technologies needed by Ethiopian farmers. 
The Opportunity 

Are you passionate about improving livestock productivity and strengthening market systems to deliver sustainable development outcomes in Ethiopia? We are seeking a Livestock Productivity Specialist for the Oromia Region to lead the implementation of interventions that enhance livestock productivity and support inclusive market growth. Reporting to the Livestock Productivity Lead, you will work closely with public and private sector partners, market actors, and other stakeholders to identify opportunities, address systemic constraints, and promote sustainable access to productivity-enhancing inputs, technologies, and services. 

 Key Responsibilities 

The Regional Livestock Productivity Specialists will spearhead the implementation of interventions that promote demand creation and utilization of livestock productivity enhancement inputs, technologies, and practices within their respective regions. The specialists will collaborate closely with livestock producers and enterprises, including poultry farms, dairy operations, feedlots, milk collection and marketing cooperatives, producer groups, livestock traders, and unions, to advance the adoption of animal health services, quality feed and fodder, and livestock genetic improvement technologies, thereby strengthening the productivity and competitiveness of Ethiopian livestock producers. 

Primary Responsibilities 

Lead the regional level capacity-building initiatives, including training programs for livestock producers to enhance effective utilization of animal health services, feed and fodder innovations, and genetic improvement technologies across dairy, poultry, beef, and sheep and goat value chains. 
Design and deliver training and refresher programs for community-level service providers- including animal health workers, private veterinary pharmacies, artificial inseminators, feed mixers, and other livestock service providers, to strengthen the delivery and uptake of quality veterinary, genetic improvement, and feed/fodder inputs and services. 
Organize and facilitate regional-level field demonstration days, learning events, and stakeholder engagement platforms to promote knowledge exchange and best practice dissemination. 
Support the design and implementation of targeted Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) campaigns, including trade fairs and promotional events, to accelerate the adoption of improved livestock production technologies and management practices, with emphasis on climate-smart solutions. 
Collaborate closely with regional market analysis and financial access specialists to facilitate market linkages among producers, input suppliers, aggregators, traders, processors, and both domestic and export buyers. 
Contribute to policy dialogue, learning events, and analytical efforts aimed at improving the enabling environment for access to and adoption of veterinary, feed, and genetic improvement inputs and technologies. 
Ensure all interventions adhere to facilitative market system development (MSD) principles, with strong emphasis on sustainability, scalability, inclusion, and reduced reliance on project support. 
Monitor, document, and report progress on the utilization of veterinary inputs, feed and fodder, and genetic improvement technologies in alignment with USDA P4P performance indicators for quarterly, biannual, and annual reports and work planning processes. 
Collaborate with strategic partners such as AfriScout and Heifer International at the regional level to integrate livestock input supply and utilization data with complementary digital solutions. 
Serve as a regional focal point for communications, coordination, and partnerships with regional government authorities and other stakeholders, representing the P4P project to maximize uptake of livestock productivity-enhancing solutions. 
Perform other related duties as assigned. 

About You
Qualifications 

Education & Experience 

BSc degree in Animal Science, Agribusiness, Agricultural Extension, or Veterinary Science (DVM), or a related field, with a minimum of 10 years of relevant professional experience; OR 
MSc degree in a related field with at least 5 years of relevant experience in livestock development, agribusiness, or agricultural extension programs. 
Professional Experience 

Proven track record working with producer groups, private livestock enterprises, dairy and livestock marketing cooperatives, agricultural aggregators, feed mills, agro dealers, veterinary service providers, and public-private extension systems. 
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities efficiently, both independently and collaboratively, under tight deadlines. 
Core Competencies 

Donor-Funded Project Experience: Prior involvement in donor-funded livestock development and marketing projects, preferably in the target regions. Experience with USAID and/or USDA-funded projects is a significant advantage. 
Technical Expertise: Demonstrated proficiency in Market Systems Development (MSD), private sector engagement strategies, and cooperative development and management. 
Relationship Management: Proven ability to build strong, trust-based relationships with private sector actors, livestock producer groups, cooperatives, and public institutions. 
Language Proficiency: This position is open exclusively to Ethiopian nationals. Fluency in English is required; proficiency in Amharic and Afan Oromo is an added advantage. 
Sector Knowledge: Strong understanding of the challenges and opportunities within poultry, dairy, beef, and sheep and goat value chains in Ethiopia, particularly in the target regions. 

Requirement Skill
Communication
